data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 7db1c5e7b76cfbcc096c5ad834350a9a843cd7de (post f593-183b fix on main)
* **CI run:** 25475541901 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/25475541901)

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

When a STATUS event is processed for a ticket that has no SYNC marker yet (i.e. the ticket was never linked to Jira via a successful CREATE), the bridge should retroactively trigger a CREATE so the latest status is reflected, OR emit a BRIDGE_ALERT and queue the ticket for the next CREATE attempt — not silently drop the STATUS event with only a WARNING-level log line.

#### Actual Behavior

Backfill run 25475541901 logged the following pattern repeatedly:

```
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-bdk5: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-cvtx: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-cnj5: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-5rya: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-9l2x: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
... (many more)
```

The handler at `plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/_outbound_handlers.py:189-200` (the `STATUS event dropped: no SYNC.json marker` branch) writes a BRIDGE_ALERT but does NOT trigger a retroactive CREATE for the ticket. Net effect: tickets that should have been created in Jira during a CREATE handler that failed earlier (e.g. the abort path that f593-183b just fixed, or a transient acli error) are now in a permanent split-brain state — the local tracker shows their latest status, but Jira has no record of them at all.

The pattern is asymmetric to the `delete` branch: when STATUS=deleted is dispatched on a ticket without a SYNC marker, the handler at line 145 logs `synced to Jira; skipping deletion` and returns — that case is benign because the ticket is already gone. But for STATUS=open|in_progress|closed without a SYNC marker, dropping the event hides real divergence.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* Triggered backfill via `gh workflow run outbound-bridge.yml -f backfill=true` (run 25475541901)
* 312 SYNC events were written successfully, but the log shows ~20+ STATUS events dropped without retroactive CREATE
* Workaround: run another backfill — the CREATE handler in backfill mode is idempotent via `has_existing_sync`, so any retry that lands the CREATE will let the next STATUS event find the SYNC marker and propagate. But this is brittle and depends on the next CREATE not being filtered out by the HEAD~1..HEAD window in non-backfill mode.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/_outbound_handlers.py:189-200 (STATUS dropped no-SYNC branch)
* plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/_outbound_handlers.py — STATUS handler dispatcher

### 6. Logs

```
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-bdk5: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
WARNING: STATUS event dropped for dso-cvtx: no SYNC.json marker — ticket has never been linked to Jira
... (~20+ similar lines in CI run 25475541901)
```

#### Suggested fix scope

In the `STATUS event dropped: no SYNC.json marker` branch of `handle_status_event`:

1. Look up the ticket directory's most-recent CREATE event.
2. If a CREATE event exists, treat the STATUS event as a trigger for retroactive CREATE: call the CREATE handler with the ticket's current state, then re-dispatch the STATUS event so the Jira issue is brought to the right status in a single bridge run.
3. If no CREATE event exists at all (truly orphan tracker dir), keep the BRIDGE_ALERT and skip — but this case should be very rare and is the only legitimate "drop" path.

Alternative: keep the current "drop and alert" behavior but add a separate scheduled job that scans for `BRIDGE_ALERT.json` files with `reason="STATUS event dropped: no SYNC.json marker"` and re-queues the originating ticket through the CREATE handler. This decouples the latency-of-fix from the bridge's per-tick window.
data.title: [bridge-outbound]: STATUS event dropped when SYNC marker missing -> tickets without prior CREATE are permanently desynced
